name: Orange 9mm
label: Revelation
lede: Burn's singer and a guitarist who'd watched him swing a hatchet on stage wanted hardcore that grooved like A Tribe Called Quest, and two major labels paid to find out if it would sell.

eras.title: A hatchet at the Anthrax
eras.text: Burn was winding down when Chaka Malik met guitarist Chris Traynor at a Burn show in Connecticut. They built Orange 9mm on a strange three-way blueprint (A Tribe Called Quest, Smashing Pumpkins, Screaming Trees) and made one EP for Revelation that still sounds like the band they meant to be.

years.h: Chaka Malik and Chris Traynor meet at a Burn show
years.p: At a [[Burn|502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6]] show at the Anthrax in Connecticut, Chaka Malik performs with a hatchet. Chris Traynor, watching, is impressed, and the two plan a new band that same day.
years.xp: Malik told No Echo that Traynor probably thought he was a little crazy. The target sound was specific: the good vibes of A Tribe Called Quest with the whimsy and heaviness of Smashing Pumpkins, plus Screaming Trees.

years.h: Orange 9mm's first rhythm section: Larry Gorman and Eric Rice
years.p: Drummer Larry Gorman comes in through Chris Traynor, his bandmate in Fountainhead, with Eric Rice on bass. Gorman leaves soon after the EP is recorded; Davide Gentile later takes over bass.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Orange 9mm EP, the rhino record · Revelation REV 31
years.p: After a demo with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]], Revelation's Jordan Cooper asks for more songs. Four tracks, cut fast, under a rhino photo shot by Chaka Malik's father, Jack Harris.
years.xp: After labouring over lyrics in Burn, Malik decided to just write. Revelation's pressing notes say a little under half of the 300 color copies came out salmon rather than orange/white swirl, and a later run of 553 dark green had three light green strays, a plant mistake.

eras.title: EastWest and the Alice in Chains producer
eras.text: One EP was enough for a major label. EastWest put Orange 9mm with Dave Jerden, who'd made records for Alice in Chains and Jane's Addiction, and sent them on the road with the new heavy bands. When sales disappointed, the label shelved them.

q: The EP sounds nothing like the album.
years.p: Produced by Dave Jerden at El Dorado in Los Angeles and Right Track in New York, with Davide Gentile on bass and Matthew Cross on drums. It reaches No. 17 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: AllMusic called it a very strong effort that belongs among the important '90s aggro and hardcore records. Chaka Malik has been harder on it: he told No Echo the album was trying to be something the band wasn't.

years.p: The hardcore kids from New York end up on bills with the rising heavy bands of the mid-'90s, and on a tour with [[Ned's Atomic Dustbin|5ecee847-839a-4b9e-aae1-0e3b5dcea2ea]].

years.h: EastWest shelves Orange 9mm after weak sales
years.p: According to Perfect Sound Forever, Driver Not Included sold below expectations and EastWest shelved the band, before moving them over to Atlantic.

eras.title: Tragic, and Helmet takes the guitarist
eras.text: Atlantic gave Orange 9mm a second shot with Barkmarket's Dave Sardy producing. The album was their most acclaimed, and within weeks its main songwriter on guitar had joined Helmet. A year later Atlantic let them go, deep in debt to the label.

years.p: Produced by Dave Sardy across three New York studios, including Chung King. Chris Traynor plays most of the bass after Davide Gentile's exit, and Taylor McLam joins near the end of the sessions.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Tragic reached No. 44 on the Heatseekers chart and sold over 47,000 copies in the US. The sound moved toward rap metal, with 7 and Method among the fan favorites.

years.h: Chris Traynor leaves Orange 9mm to join [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]]
years.p: Shortly after Tragic comes out, Chris Traynor walks mid-promotion to tour with Helmet. Taylor McLam moves over to guitar.

years.big: Two major-label records and a hole they couldn't climb out of
years.h: Atlantic drops Orange 9mm over unrecouped costs
years.p: Two albums and a lot of tour support later, Atlantic lets Orange 9mm go. Taylor McLam said a band in that spot owed the label for every tour it had fronted.
years.xp: McLam told Perfect Sound Forever that if you made two major-label records and didn't pay back the tour support, you were deep in the hole. The band kept going on an independent label.

eras.title: Loops, Warped Tour and the end
eras.text: Orange 9mm finished on an indie, Ng Records, and tried something new: less hardcore, more rapping over loops and electronics. It didn't sell, the touring wore them down, and they split in 2000.

years.p: Chaka Malik, Taylor McLam and Matthew Cross throw out every demo and start fresh at Mad Dog in Burbank with producer Neil Perry. Malik plays bass himself.
years.xp: Recorded March to April 1999, with Sacha Jenkins on backing vocals. The Ultraman vs. Godzilla EP also came out on Ng around this time. Wikipedia calls the album a commercial disappointment.

years.h: Orange 9mm on the Warped Tour and with [[Machine Head|22a1f4d7-81ff-4216-ac06-3387da6bc118]]
years.p: Orange 9mm tour Pretend I'm Human on the 1999 Warped Tour and on dates with Machine Head.

q: The music business can beat you down.
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · No Echo · Wikipedia
years.p: Taylor McLam said the band just wasn't feeling it anymore. Chaka Malik later said Orange 9mm had three albums with nine different sounds.

eras.title: Ghost Decibels and the remasters
eras.text: Chris Traynor went on to Helmet and later Bush; Taylor McLam moved into commercial music and started High Desert Fires with Traynor. Chaka Malik came back with an electronic project, and the Orange 9mm records started coming back out.

years.h: Chaka Malik returns with Ghost Decibels
years.p: Orange 9mm's singer comes back to music with an electronic project, Ghost Decibels.

years.h: Pretend I'm Human reissued, guitars turned up
years.p: RevHQ Records and Thirty Something Records remaster Orange 9mm's last album, fixing what Chaka Malik always said was wrong with it: the guitars were too low.
Orange 9mm's late Ng Records EP comes out in a 2023 remaster on streaming services.

eras.title: Twenty-five years later, on a rooftop
eras.text: Chaka Malik and Taylor McLam brought Orange 9mm back with a new rhythm section, and without Chris Traynor, who was still in Bush.

years.h: Orange 9mm reform with Cory Bonfiglio and Chris Enríquez
years.p: Chaka Malik and Taylor McLam announce the reunion, with Cory Bonfiglio on bass and Chris Enríquez on drums.

years.h: First Orange 9mm show in 25 years: the NYC Tattoo Convention
years.p: Orange 9mm play the Terminal 5 rooftop during the New York City Tattoo Arts Convention, their first show since 1999.
